question: How does Rachel Carson open Silent Spring?
answer: With 'A Fable for Tomorrow': an American town where, one spring, the birds no longer sing, livestock sicken and orchards bear no fruit, all because of a white powder that fell from the sky. Carson explained that no single town had suffered every harm, but each had happened somewhere.
move: A vivid story can make scattered evidence impossible to ignore.
simply: Carson started with an imaginary town where spring is silent because the birds have died. Every disaster in it had really happened somewhere.
why: Gathering scattered harms into one picture is how many problems first get noticed. Carson said plainly that her town was imaginary: good advocacy marks where fact ends.

book.title: Silent Spring
book.author: Rachel Carson
book.badge: Credited with starting the modern environmental movement

reference: Rachel Carson, Silent Spring (Houghton Mifflin, 1962), ch. 1
